neighbours.label: content words inside lines of rhymed, metrical verse (poems, hymns, ballads), as opposed to the same content in prose
fire:
The river ran beside the mill,
The miller's wife was singing still;
She sang of love and sang of loss,
Of golden fields and graves of moss.

When I was young and full of cheer,
I roamed the hills from year to year;
But now my legs are slow and lame,
And every season feels the same.

O Lord, who made the stars to shine,
And set the moon in heaven's line,
Look down upon thy servant here,
And keep me safe from every fear.

The soldier marched through rain and snow,
He had a thousand miles to go;
He thought of home and of his bride,
And of the farm on the hillside.

Farewell, my friends, I must away,
The ship departs at break of day;
And though the sea be wide and grey,
I'll think of you when far I stray.

There was a maid in Lincoln town,
Who wore a red and silken gown;
The squire saw her at the fair,
And lost his heart to her dark hair.

The autumn leaves are falling fast,
The summer days are gone at last;
The swallows gather on the eaves,
And fly away from barren sheaves.

My mother sat beside the fire,
And sang the songs of the old choir;
Her voice was soft, her hands were worn,
She'd laboured since the day was born.
quiet: The river ran beside the old mill, and the miller's wife often sang there about love, loss, the fields and the cemetery.
When I was young I walked the hills every year, but my legs are slow now and the seasons all feel alike.
We ask God, who made the stars and the moon, to look after his followers and keep them safe from harm.
The soldier marched for weeks through rain and snow, thinking about his wife and the family farm back home.
I said goodbye to my friends because the ship was leaving early in the morning, and I promised to write.
A young woman from Lincoln wore a red silk dress to the fair, where the local squire noticed her.
The leaves are falling quickly now that summer is over, and the swallows are gathering before they migrate.
My mother used to sit by the fire singing hymns she had learned in the choir, her hands worn from work.
